description:
Port-map §3. Pure-ish state machine that accumulates bytes from
Terminal (.2) and emits complete escape sequences + plain chars.

- OctoPi.Tui.StdinFSM GenServer.
- handle_call({:process, chunk}, _, state):
    new_buffer = state.buffer <> chunk
    {seqs, remainder} = extract_complete_sequences(new_buffer)
    broadcast seqs via OctoPi.Tui.Events
    timeout = if remainder == "", do: :infinity, else: @flush_ms
    {:reply, :ok, %{state | buffer: remainder}, timeout}
- handle_info(:timeout, %{buffer: ""}) → no-op
- handle_info(:timeout, %{buffer: buf}) → flush buf as-is

Sequence detection (multi-head pattern matching, not cond/case
at the top of one function):
- CSI: "\e[..." ends on byte 0x40-0x7E
- OSC: "\e]..." ends on BEL or ST ("\e\\")
- Meta: "\e<char>" (single char after ESC)
- Bracketed paste: "\e[200~" ... "\e[201~"
- SS3: "\eO<char>"
- Plain char: anything not starting with ESC

Mirrors upstream stdin-buffer.test.ts (port-map §14.1) — 422
lines of cases: split-across-chunks, timeout-flush, SGR mouse,
old X11 mouse, arrows, function keys, Kitty press/release,
bracketed paste, flush/destroy.

TDD: lift the whole case list from §14.1.

Depends on .1. Can be built independently of .2 (tested directly
with `:process` calls).
title: Stdin FSM: escape-sequence assembly + GenServer timeout flush
